newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's primary Cetes rates fall for second week.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's primary Cetes rates fall for second week.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rates fell for the second straight week at Banco de Mexico's primary treasury bill auction on Monday, pulled down by expectations of lower inflation, analysts said.
The 29-day Cetes rate fell by 111 basis points to 20.59 percent from last week's 21.70 percent for 28-day paper, the central bank said.
The fall was greater than expected. Money market dealers surveyed by Reuters earlier in the day forecast a decline of 66 basis points on the one-month paper.
Analysts said the market already had discounted any decline in interest rates in the United States, before the Federal Reserve's open market committee meeting this week.
"They have totally discounted any moves by the Fed, and to this we have to add the good inflation numbers," Jaime Hernandez, an analyst with consulting firm Asesoria Estrategica, told Reuters.
The key one-month Cetes rate fell by 147 basis points at the auction the week before.

Nervous investors had pushed the one-month rate up by 458 basis points at the two auctions on March 4 and March 11 after a 10-week decline that brought rates to their lowest levels since the 1994 peso crash.
Investors appear, however, to have regained their sense of confidence in Mexico, cheered once again by expectations of lower inflation and the newfound stability in the foreign exchange market.
That optimism received a boost on Monday by a report from the central bank that said the consumer price index for the first two weeks of March rose by 0.66 percent, slightly below expectations.
Valores Finamex noted in a report on Monday that in the first two months of the year, inflation left Mexican investors with negative real interest rates.

"However, we estimate that during March there has been a real return due to the rebound of rates in the first weeks of the month and the expectations of inflation lower than that seen in the last four months," the brokerage said.
Valores Finamex is forecasting a real return of 5.3 percent for the year, based on inflation of 18 percent for the year.

Demand remained strong at the auction this week as investors sought 15.05 billion pesos worth of Cetes. There were 3.0 billion pesos worth on offer. That compared to demand of 15.07 billion the week before.
The auction was held a day earlier than usual because of the Easter holiday.
